newsitem.title: USA: Freeport Copper signs pact for Busang stake.
newsitem.headline: Freeport Copper signs pact for Busang stake.

text.p: Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc said Thursday it has signed a binding agreement to acquire a 15 percent interest in two Indonesian companies to be formed that are expected to be granted contracts to explore and develop mining rights in the Busang II and Busang III areas of Indonesia.
The agreement was signed with Bre-X Minerals Ltd, its partner in the venture.
The companies to be formed will be owned 45 percent by Bre-X, 40 percent by Indonesian interests including the government of Indonesia and 15 percent by Freeport-McMoran.
Under the deal, Freeport-McMoran is to be the sole operator of the Busang II and Busang III properties.

In consideration for the transaction, Freeport-McMoran has agreed to provide 25 percent of the total estimated cost of delineating a proven reserve and constructing the initial Busang mine complex, up to $400 million.

In addition, it has agreed to arrange, on behalf of the Indonesian companies, a $1.2 billion project financing commitment from Chase Manhattan Corp for the remaining estimated costs of the initial Busang mine complex.

The company said it has undertaken a due diligence review of the Busang gold properties and expects to begin preparation of a feasibility study during the second quarter of 1997 that will form the basis for the initial mine and mill development. The development has an initial production objective of 100,000 to 150,000 metric tonnes of ore per day, it said.
It said it will try to minimize the environmental impacts of the Busang mine.
